title: A Tide for the Bakery
premise: Sable Lockridge has spent a decade keeping her late grandfather's lighthouse, writing novels under a pseudonym, and avoiding the town of Merrow Point that once branded her family thieves. When a clerical error places her name alongside Jonah Vane's—the son of the man who ruined hers—on the deed to a derelict orchard, neither can sell without the other's signature. Forced into uneasy partnership restoring the orchard before the vineyard consortium buys it out from under them, Sable uncovers evidence that her grandfather was framed, and that Jonah's father confessed it in letters Jonah never read. As harvest nears, Sable must choose between legal vindication that would destroy Jonah's family name and a quieter justice that lets them both keep something. She signs the deed over to a community land trust, publishes the truth as fiction, and finally lets Jonah stay past the last train.
about_author: Ines Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing coastal property disputes before turning them into love stories. She lives within sight of a decommissioned lighthouse and writes each morning before the fog lifts.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes her solitary rhythm at the lighthouse: tending the light, drafting her third novel, dodging invitations from town. A certified letter arrives from the county recorder. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation beginning to crack; she reads the letter three times and doesn't sleep.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Line
chapters.summary: Sable travels to the county office and discovers the deed to Hollow Orchard lists both her and Jonah Vane as co-owners—a recording error twenty years old. The clerk offers no easy fix. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into stubbornness; she decides to confront the problem rather than flee it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He arrives in Merrow Point intending a quick signature and quicker exit, carrying his father's recent death and a box of unopened effects. He finds Sable waiting at the orchard gate with a lawyer's letter. Emotional beat: guilt he can't name meeting resentment he can.

chapters.title: Terms of Hostility
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Their first negotiation collapses—Sable wants him gone, Jonah wants to sell fast to the Bellamy Vineyard Group. Neither can act alone. They agree to a temporary truce: assess the property together for thirty days. Emotional beat: grudging truce, both lying about their real intentions.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Walking the overgrown rows, she finds her grandfather's grafting marks still alive on half-dead trees—and realizes he never abandoned the orchard after the scandal; he tended it secretly. Emotional beat: grief reframing itself as inheritance; her anger at Jonah softens toward confusion.

chapters.title: Letters Unopened
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sorting his father's box, he finds sealed letters addressed to 'E. Lockridge' that were never sent, plus a ledger with suspicious entries dated the year of the theft accusation. He hides the ledger. Emotional beat: loyalty to a dead father warring with dawning suspicion.

chapters.title: Rain on the Roof Beams
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A storm traps them in the orchard's collapsing barn overnight while repairing the roof. Stranded by washed-out roads, they talk for the first time honestly—her pseudonymous novels, his failed marriage, why they both left. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared shelter; walls lowering.

chapters.title: The Consortium Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Bellamy Vineyard's representative, Dana Okafor, presents a generous buyout contingent on clear title—which requires Sable's cooperation or a quiet lawsuit. Jonah stalls, not admitting why. Emotional beat: temptation versus the first thing he's wanted to protect in years.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Working the trees together, she teaches Jonah her grandfather's methods; he proves unexpectedly patient. Townspeople begin noticing them, reviving old gossip about the Lockridge scandal. Emotional beat: belonging she'd sworn off, shadowed by the town's long memory.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ruthie Calloway, retired town librarian, reveals she kept clippings and a statement her grandfather made before his death claiming innocence—and naming a witness who died conveniently soon after. Emotional beat: hope arriving like contraband; Sable begins investigating in earnest.

chapters.title: A Signature Withheld
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sable asks Jonah directly whether his father ever spoke of the orchard. He lies. That night he reads one unsent letter: his father describing the frame-up in fragments, too cowardly to confess fully. Emotional beat: shame compounding; he can't confess without destroying his father's memory.

chapters.title: First Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The consortium moves up its deadline, threatening litigation that would freeze the property and expose everything publicly. Sable and Jonah argue bitterly—she accuses him of stalling, he accuses her of wanting a spectacle. Emotional beat: midpoint rupture; trust fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ruthie helps Sable decode the stolen ledger (slipped anonymously into her mailbox) showing payments routed through the orchard the year of the theft—payments matching what her grandfather was accused of stealing. Emotional beat: vindication and fury entwined; the truth has a shape now.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah realizes Sable has the ledger and that going public will bury his father's name. He offers her a private confession and a public apology in exchange for silence. She refuses: justice hidden isn't justice. Emotional beat: two definitions of mercy colliding head-on.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Jonah packs to leave, signing everything over to her. At the station platform, Sable arrives—not to stop him, but to give him the unsent letters, saying he deserves to know his father loved him even while failing everyone else. Emotional beat: heartbreak offered freely instead of weaponized.

chapters.title: Bud Break
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Instead of boarding, Jonah stays the night reading every letter, then walks to the lighthouse at dawn. He tells Sable he'll testify—not to save his father's name, but because she shouldn't carry the truth alone anymore. Emotional beat: surrender as the beginning of trust.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Before the county board, Jonah presents the ledger and letters; Ruthie and others corroborate. The 20-year-old judgment against E. Lockridge is vacated. The town must reckon with what it did to a dead man and his granddaughter. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; some apologies arrive decades late.

chapters.title: Bellamy's Countermove
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The consortium, embarrassed, threatens to sue over title irregularities anyway—unless the co-owners sell cheap. Sable proposes an alternative: a community land trust, with the town's newly ashamed leading families pressured to fund it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, built from leverage and nerve.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The whole town turns out for the first harvest—scrappy, imperfect, real. Sable and Jonah work the last row together as the light fades. Almost-touches, unfinished sentences. Emotional beat: tenderness deferred so long it aches; everything hangs on one conversation.

chapters.title: The Chapter She Almost Cut
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable admits she's been writing their story into her novel under thin disguises—and that in every draft she ended it before the confession because she didn't believe she'd get one. Jonah asks to hear how she'd write it if she believed. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the true climax; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The final train passes the orchard crossing. Jonah doesn't watch it go. Sable asks him to stay—not for the season, but indefinitely. He says yes before she finishes asking. Emotional beat: the second chance she never believed in, accepted at last.

chapters.title: A Tide for the Bakery
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. One year later: the orchard thrives under the land trust, the lighthouse is a museum where Sable leads tours, and her new novel—published under her real name—is dedicated to 'the man who stayed.' The bakery on the corner names a loaf after the tide schedule. Emotional beat: full-circle peace; visibility chosen, home claimed.
